blocks.text: MANILA, Philippines – Situated squarely within the tropical solar belt, the Philippines receives an average of 4.5 to 5.5 kilowatt-hours of solar radiation per square meter per day. Yet, fossil fuels continue to dominate the nation’s power grid, with coal alone generating roughly 62% of its electricity, according to Department of Energy data cited by engineering firm REURASIA. Structural, financial, and policy bottlenecks kept solar on the margins, and it still accounts for under 4 percent of national power consumption, according to government data.
